answer: Trust propagates through a transition kernel by bounded-length random walks rooted in established attestations, so voting weight reflects reachable trust rather than claimed identities. A sybil cluster—even one that can forge internal attestations, such as the violet group—has limited influence when its boundary is sparse: for cluster S, conductance Φ(S)=w(∂S)/vol(S) bounds the probability of exiting S per step. Thus, from honest roots, its aggregate reachable vote is constrained by the walk horizon and boundary flow.
